evidence.observation: BuildQueue owns a Map<string, SerialQueue> keyed by asset id (line 12). Each distinct key lazily gets exactly one SerialQueue (lines 16-20), so all submissions for the same asset share a single concurrency-1 lane. This is the per-asset single-flight mechanism: duplicate submissions for one asset are serialized rather than run concurrently, which is what keeps duplicate builds from doing conflicting concurrent work over the same git/SQLite/files resources.

enqueue(key, job) is fire-and-forget: it reuses the key's existing SerialQueue or creates one, then adds the job and swallows rejection (lines 21-23). Note the contract precisely: enqueue does NOT drop duplicate jobs — it preserves FIFO order and guarantees non-overlap. Duplicate work is therefore averted by the caller's admission/checkpoint layer (wiki-service), while BuildQueue supplies the no-concurrent-duplicate guarantee at the queue level.

onIdle(key?) awaits a single key's queue or, with no argument, Promise.all over every per-asset queue (line 32). This is the deterministic drain point that makes the contract testable: after onIdle() no build job for any asset is still pending or running, so 'effective work' counts are stable and observable.

The concurrency=1 engine reached through BuildQueue. drain() returns early when already running (line 82), shifts one entry, sets running=true, and only re-drains after the task settles (lines 91-99). Two jobs on the same per-asset queue can never overlap, confirming the single-flight guarantee BuildQueue delegates to.

Admission control for build submission. If the asset is already pending or processing (lines 276-278) ingest returns {kind:"busy"} without writing status, without an audit row, and crucially without calling enqueueBuild — so a duplicate build submission never reaches the queue. Only a non-busy submission bumps the version, sets pending, and enqueues exactly one build (lines 279-288).

Build worker entry/exit checkpoints. The entry checkpoint (lines 1016-1019) calls isDeleted and returns before any worker invocation, so a job queued for an asset that has since been deleted produces zero effective work. The end checkpoint (lines 1039-1042) prevents committing ready/audit/callback state for an asset deleted mid-run. Together they make queued duplicates no-ops once the asset is gone.

The single call site that bridges submission to the queue: it enqueues under row.wiki_id — the asset id — which is exactly the key BuildQueue partitions on. This is why two submissions for the same wiki land on the same SerialQueue lane and can never run concurrently.

The worker checkpoint predicate: deleted if the cancelled flag is set or the metadata row no longer exists. The dual criterion covers both delete-during-run and delete-before-the-checkpoint orderings, letting runBuild skip a duplicate job without doing work.

Source-submission idempotency. Query-then-update, not a blind UPSERT: unknown filename INSERTs as 'uploaded' (lines 227-232); a changed sha256 UPDATEs and resets to 'uploaded' (lines 234-240); an unchanged sha256 returns 'unchanged' with no write at all (line 241). Re-uploading identical source content therefore does not reset the row's ingested state and provokes no re-ingest — duplicate source submission is inert.

The caller that makes source submission idempotent: it hashes each uploaded file with sha256 (line 893) and calls upsertSource inside one write transaction (lines 889-898). Registering duplicate identical content hits the 'unchanged' branch and changes nothing, so a duplicate upload does not queue additional ingest work.

claims.claim: Duplicate build submissions for the same asset cannot execute concurrently: BuildQueue partitions jobs by asset key into one SerialQueue each (concurrency=1), so a repeated submission is serialized behind the in-flight build rather than run in parallel over the same git/SQLite/files resources.

BuildQueue.enqueue does not itself deduplicate jobs — it preserves and serializes them; the guarantee that a duplicate submission yields no duplicate effective work is completed by the caller: wiki-service.ingest rejects pending/processing duplicates as busy without enqueuing, and runBuild's isDeleted entry checkpoint turns any queued duplicate whose asset was deleted into a no-op worker invocation.
enqueueBuild keys the queue by wiki_id (the asset id), which is the exact key BuildQueue partitions on, so every submission for one wiki shares a single concurrency-1 lane.

Duplicate SOURCE submission with identical content is idempotent: upsertSource compares the stored sha256 and returns 'unchanged' without any write, and registerSources hashes each upload before calling it, so re-uploading the same content neither resets the source row nor provokes a rebuild.
BuildQueue.onIdle drains every per-asset queue, giving a deterministic observation point at which total effective-work counts (worker invocations) for duplicate submissions can be measured.

conclusion: Proven: in MemoryKnowledge a duplicate source or build submission does not create duplicate effective work. The defense is layered. (1) Build submission admission — wiki-service.ingest (src/store/wiki-service.ts:272-290) rejects a submission while the asset is pending/processing with {kind:"busy"} and never calls enqueueBuild, so the duplicate never becomes a queued job; the executed demo shows 3 rapid submissions producing exactly 1 worker invocation. (2) Queue-level single-flight — BuildQueue (src/store/build-queue.ts:11-34) lazily maps each asset id to one SerialQueue whose drain has concurrency=1 (src/store/serial-queue.ts:81-101), so even when duplicate jobs do reach the queue (e.g. a race past admission) they run strictly one-at-a-time, never overlapped, as the real-source demo asserts (maxConcurrent=1 against 5 duplicate same-key jobs). (3) Worker checkpoints — runBuild (src/store/wiki-service.ts:1014-1077) checks isDeleted at entry (1016-1019) and exit (1039-1042), so a duplicate job queued for an asset deleted before or during the run performs zero worker invocations and commits nothing. (4) Source submission idempotency — upsertSource (src/engines/wiki/index-db.ts:219-242) returns 'unchanged' for an identical sha256 without writing and without resetting the row's ingested state, so re-uploading the same content provokes no re-ingest. Scope note: BuildQueue serializes but does not drop duplicates; the no-duplicate-work guarantee is architectural across the queue plus its callers, not a property of build-queue.ts alone. The contract is captured executably in .prale-eval/demo.mjs: 15/15 assertions pass, exit code 0.
